subject: Renewal + Expansion: proposal for co-term + ceiling credit
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mike Santos <mike@cedarbridge.com>, Anika Rao <anika.rao@cedarbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + Expansion: proposal for co-term + ceiling credit

Hi Mike / Anika —

Thanks again for the productive renewal conversation last week. Per our call, CedarBridge is planning to add 120M embedding units as part of the renewal window. To make the procurement timeline smooth and align billing, we propose the following:

1) Co-term the new capacity to CedarBridge's existing contract anniversary (Jan 1) so everything invoices together.
2) Apply a one-time ceiling credit of $40,000 to offset near-term overage risk during the first 60 days post-add.
3) Maintain the quoted uplift pricing (20% list uplift for the additional units) but offer a 2% additional discount if CedarBridge commits to a 12-month annualized capacity minimum for the add-on.

Attached: Amendment_draft_v1.pdf (redlines + pricing appendix).

Can you confirm: (a) whether procurement needs a specific co-term effective date (you mentioned Jan 1 on the call), and (b) if PO timing (you noted late April) aligns with getting the amendment signed and live? If yes, I can route an updated amendment and a DocuSign link today.

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwoodinference.com

From: Mike Santos <mike@cedarbridge.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Anika Rao <anika.rao@cedarbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal + Expansion: proposal for co-term + ceiling credit

Priyom —

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from procurement:

- We do want a Jan 1 co-term, but procurement requires an effective start date and an explicit monthly cap for the first billing quarter (they want to avoid surprise overages in Q1).
- The $40k credit is helpful. Question: can that credit be applied across the first two invoices rather than as a single lump sum? That makes forecasting easier for our finance team.
- If you can increase the discount another 1–2% (or structure a volume band that steps down pricing as we hit certain thresholds) that will speed PO approval.

PO timeline: procurement is targeting a PO in hand by 30 Apr. Legal will do a fast review but they will need an unambiguous amendment and clear billing schedule.

Appreciate the help — if we can get the doc and the breakdown of how the credit is applied, we can likely get this through.

—Mike
Head of Platform Ops | CedarBridge Inc.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal + Expansion: proposal for co-term + ceiling credit

Forwarding Mike's procurement asks. Quick thoughts on options to present (leaning toward #A to keep momentum):

Option A (preferred, lower approval friction):
- Keep $40k ceiling credit, but split it across the first two invoices (apply $20k to invoice 1 and $20k to invoice 2).
- Explicit monthly cap for first quarter = prorated expected usage + a 15% buffer (we should propose a concrete number based on their expected 120M units).
- No additional permanent list discount; instead offer a one-time 2% rebate applied MID-YEAR if commit is met at 6 months.

Option B (trade for term):
- Apply $40k credit as lump sum + additional 2% list discount for a 12-month committed minimum on the add-on (requires finance approval).

Option C (banding):
- Offer stepped pricing bands (0–40M / 40–80M / 80–120M) to give them visibility; more complex for billing.

Ben — can you confirm if finance will sign off on Option B authority (2% off list for 12-month commit)? Lauren — can you OK Option A as sales-approved fallback so we can keep the PO timeline?

Marissa
Sr. Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal + Expansion: proposal for co-term + ceiling credit

Marissa / team —

I approve Option A as the primary path. Conditions:
- Credit split across two invoices is acceptable.
- We need Legal to confirm amended language around the monthly cap and the amortization of the credit so there are no misunderstandings.
- Finance will review the 2% rebate structure if they hit commit at 6 months; do not promise the rebate until finance confirms.

Ben — please loop Finance (cc'd earlier) for a quick nod on the numbers; we should not delay the DocuSign link. Priyom — please update the amendment with: explicit co-term effective date (2028-01-01), monthly cap table for Q1 (propose numbers in the amendment based on the 120M add), and the 2-invoice credit schedule. Then route to Legal for final redline.

Lauren
VP Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mike Santos <mike@cedarbridge.com>, Anika Rao <anika.rao@cedarbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + Expansion: proposal for co-term + ceiling credit

Hi Mike / Anika —

Per our internal review, CedarBridge and Redwood can proceed with the following agreed items:

- Co-term effective date: 2028-01-01 (amendment will show the new capacity added with the Jan 1 co-term).
- Ceiling credit: $40,000 one-time, applied as $20,000 credit to first invoice after amendment goes live and $20,000 to the second invoice (explicit schedule in amendment).
- Monthly cap for Q1: we propose a cap of 45M embedding units per month for Jan–Mar (this is the expected usage + ~15% buffer). Amendment includes an overage rate and a one-time pricing reconciliation clause to be used only if usage exceeds the cap for two consecutive months.
- Additional 2% rebate: proposed but subject to final sign-off from Finance and conditional on meeting the 6-month commit metric; will be included as a contingent clause, not automatic.

Next steps: I attached the updated amendment (Amendment_draft_v2.pdf) with those details baked in and a DocuSign link for signature: https://docusign.com/cedarbridge/amendment/12345

If procurement can get the PO to us by 30 Apr, Legal has agreed to an expedited review and we should be able to execute before month-end. Please confirm you are good with the amendment language and I will send the DocuSign envelope.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Amendment_draft_v2.pdf (redlined), pricing_summary_Q1_caps.xlsx (referenced)
